title: introduce-incremental-exemplar-profiles-and-release-note-mapper
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: onboarding churn and noisy changelogs make it hard for downstream teams to understand what actually changed between model versions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an incremental 'exemplar profile' snapshot store that keeps a tiny, representative set of inference traces for each model/version (sampling + deterministic hashing), and 2) a release-note-mapper service that turns profile deltas into short, ranked human-friendly changelog excerpts. Goals: reduce manual release note effort, surface meaningful performance/latency/capacity regressions, and provide deterministic exemplars for rollback diagnostics. Design summary: - Exemplar snapshots are produced incrementally during onboarding and periodic telemetry backfills; each snapshot contains up to 128 exemplar records (input hash, token-length bucket, trimmed KV-cache seed, perf summary). - A lightweight exemplars index (LSM-backed) stores signature -> exemplar pointers and a small bloom filter for fast delta detection. - The release-note-mapper consumes a pair of exemplar snapshots, computes a ranked delta (latency median/P95 diffs, failure-mode diffs, token-efficiency deltas), and generates a short scoring blob with rationale and suggested human blurb. - Integrations: onboarding pipeline will store snapshot metadata in model metadata, the console will surface top-3 mapped blurbs as draft release-notes, and the CLI adds --exemplar-seed to reproduce an exemplar locally. Important constraints: privacy-safe (no raw user text kept — exemplars are hashed/truncated), deterministic sampling to allow reproducible diffs, low runtime overhead (<2% CPU for ingestion path). Checklist: - [x] Incremental exemplar snapshot writer and compact on-disk format - [x] Exemplar index service + API (list/get/diff) - [x] release-note-mapper core heuristic + templating - [x] CLI flag and local reproduce tool - [x] unit + integration tests for mapper ranking heuristics - [x] docs: developer guide + console UI hints - [x] rollout plan + feature flag - [ ] e2e smoke test against a live model corpus (follow-up job created) Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag registry.exemplar.enabled, canary to 5% of onboard flows for 48 hours, expand to 25% for 72 hours, full enable after telemetry looks healthy. Linked work: ENG-2981 (exemplar sampling design), ENG-3020 (release notes automation). Security & privacy: exemplars are salted hashes + fixed-length token windows; storage TTL default 90 days and configurable. Backwards compatibility: metadata schema bump uses optional fields; consumers will ignore if absent. Migration: background backfill job (created as a follow-up) will populate exemplars for recent major releases. See docs/release-notes-mapping.md for examples and heuristics.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega (reviewer): Nice end-to-end design. Two high-level asks: (1) ensure the exemplar format is forward compatible (suggest version header + optional fields), (2) explain how bloom filters avoid false positives for the typical corpus size.

Aisha Khan (author): Addressed: added 8-byte header with version and reserved flags; adjusted LSM bloom bits and added a unit test that fakes a 10M key-space to validate false-positive rates. See ls m_store.py lines ~120-170.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Mapper heuristics look good. Request: add a small guard for noisy latency metrics (e.g., if sample size < 20, fall back to median-only blurb).
Aisha Khan (author): Implemented sample-size gating and added test cases (tests/test_release_note_mapper.py::test_small_sample_fallback).
Jared Bloom (reviewer): Important: privacy review — are we storing any raw PII? The earlier design says hashed/truncated, please document salt management and rotation.

Aisha Khan (author): Clarified in docs/release-notes-mapping.md: exemplars store salted sha256(input) + token-window (max 128 tokens) truncated by token index; salts are per-tenant and rotated via KMS integration (rotation path included). Added pointer to security review ticket SUP-412.

release_notes: Add: incremental exemplar snapshots and release-note-mapper that generate concise, ranked changelog blurbs from representative inference traces. Feature gated behind registry.exemplar.enabled. Privacy: exemplars are salted+hashed and truncated; default TTL 90 days. Rollout: canary then staged expansion.

notes_for_consumers: Console: draft release-notes UI will show top-3 mapped blurbs with 'Why this change matters' rationale. CLI: use `redwood registry reproduce --exemplar-seed <hex>` to fetch an exemplar and run locally. If you rely on older metadata, no action required; new fields are optional.
